body.t: All clients on DTG or EFV based ART
Preferred ≥14 yr & 30kg: 3HP + Vit B6 (Once-weekly Isoniazid + Rifampicin x 3mo)
Vit B6 once weekly + 3 adult tabs once weekly of 3HP (300mg INH/300mg Rifapentine)
Preferred <14 yr or <30kg: 6H + Vit B6 (Once daily Isoniazid + B6 x 6 mo). *TPT in those <12 months only if there is a new known pulmonary TB contact
*Vit B6 OD + 6H (100mg INH) dosing by weight: <5kg 0.5 OD; 5-9.9kg 1 OD; 10-13.9kg 1.5 OD; 14-19.9kg 2 OD; 20-24.9kg 2.5 OD; ≥25kg 1 adult tab (300mg)

body.section: Children initiating TB treatment while on ART

body.t: Increase DTG [note 2] to twice daily dosing. Continue current backbone.

*Maintain all dose adjustments for 2 weeks after completion of ATT. *The preferred regimen for children with DTG resistance is an optimized NRTI backbone with LPV/r [note 3]. If this is not available a holding regimen of AZT/3TC/ABC OR NNRTI based therapy may be necessary. Please consult with an expert in Paediatric HIV/TB.

Preferred: If DTG-naïve, transition to a DTG [note 2]-based regimen (with appropriate dose adjustment). Continue current backbone. Alternative: If DTG is not possible, LPV/r [note 3] dose adjustment is needed: Ritonavir (RTV) dose needs to be "super-boosted" to achieve the same dose as LPV in mg, in a ratio equal to or approaching 1:1. In older children and adolescents swallowing tablets the LPV/r dose can be doubled.
Change of regimen is needed: replace DRV/r with DTG [note 2] if DTG-naive or with LPV/r [note 3] if DTG-experienced (with appropriate dose adjustment). Continue current backbone.
Change of regimen is needed: replace ATV/r with DTG if DTG-naive or with LPV/r [note 3] if DTG-experienced (with appropriate dose adjustment). Continue current backbone.

body.section: Neonates (first 28 days of life) initiating TB treatment while on ART

body.t: Change of regimen is needed: substitute NVP as soon as possible with DTG [note 2] or LPV/r [note 3] (with appropriate dose adjustment).

footnotes: [note 1] Do not use lead in dosing and use the maximum recommended dose by neonatal dosing chart if administering with rifampicin. Transition to DTG when 3 kgs and 4 weeks of age.
[note 2] DTG should be dosed twice daily in children on TB treatment. This dose adjustment must continue for 2 weeks after completing ATT.

[note 3] If used, LPV/r dose adjustment is needed: ritonavir (RTV) dose needs to be "super-boosted" to achieve the same dose as LPV in mg, in a ratio equal to or approaching 1:1. In older children and adolescents swallowing tablets the LPV/r dose can be doubled. This dose adjustment must continue for 2 weeks after completing ATT.

tables.caption: Preferred and alternative ART in children when initiating ART in children on TB treatment
tables.caption_note: Printed as the table's title row.

header.t: Preferred first-line regimen, including initiation while on TB treatment

body.t: ABC + 3TC + DTG [note 2]; TDF + 3TC + LPV/r [note 3]; ABC + 3TC + LPV/r [note 3]

footnotes: [note 1] Do not use lead in dosing; use the maximum recommended dose by neonatal dosing chart if administering with rifampicin. Transition to DTG when 3 kgs and 4 weeks of age.
[note 2] DTG should be dosed twice daily in children on TB treatment. This dose adjustment must continue for 2 weeks after completing ATT.

[note 3] If used, LPV/r dose adjustment is needed: Ritonavir (RTV) dose needs to be "super-boosted" to achieve the same dose as LPV in mg, in a ratio equal to or approaching 1:1. In older children and adolescents swallowing tablets the LPV/r dose can be doubled. This dose adjustment must continue for 2 weeks after completing ATT.

tables.heading_path: Chapter 9: ART for Children & Adolescents > 9.7 Second Line ART for Children & Adolescents
tables.caption: Second-line ART for children and adolescents by weight and current first-line regimen
tables.caption_note: No printed title; table sits directly under heading 9.7.

body.t: *Concept: When changing to 2nd line, in most cases, it is important to change 2 drugs to maintain a robust regimen. Evidence-based exceptions include TLE to TLD and PI based regimens where the NRTI backbone can be recycled. *LPV/r can be changed to ATV/r once client is ≥40kg regardless of VL. **DRV/r can only be used for second line in cases of confirmed INSTI resistance on genotype. Consult HIVDR clinical expert committee.

Refer to National HIVDR Clinical Expert Committee. Only switch to 2nd line if genotype test (resistance test) shows DTG-resistance or PI-resistance. The 2nd line regimen should be determined by the genotype results.
ABC + 3TC + DTG; TDF + 3TC + boosted PI** (ATV/r* or LPV/r or DRV/r**)
AZT + 3TC + DTG; TDF + 3TC + boosted PI** (ATV/r* or LPV/r or DRV/r**)
AZT + 3TC + DTG; TDF + 3TC + boosted PI (ATV/r* or LPV [text cut off in the source]
TDF + 3TC + DTG; ABC + 3TC + DTG; AZT + 3TC + DTG

Refer to National HIVDR Clinical Expert Committee. Only switch to 2nd line if resistance test shows DTG resistance and the 2nd line regimen should be a boosted PI + 2 NRTIs determined by the genotype results.

tables.table_note: Children and adolescents with at least 2 consecutive detectable VL results while on DTG- or PI-based regimens should be referred to the National HIVDR Clinical Expert Committee (snapthirdline@mohcoag.com) for evaluation of drug resistance and need for genotyping. HIV genotyping (resistance testing) should be done for all clients failing on a DTG- or PI-based ART regimen. Only switch to 2nd line if the resistance test shows DTG resistance and the 2nd line regimen should be a boosted PI + 2 NRTIs determined by the genotype results.
footnotes: Refer to Annex 11.19 for the paediatrics dosing chart.
